paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. When Gibeon cried out, "Come quickly and save us!", Joshua came, and the LORD was already ahead of him. Before Israel attacked, God said, "Do not be afraid of them, for I have delivered them into your hand." (Joshua 10:6, 8) The win was promised before Israel ever struck.

Now look at what Joshua did with that promise. He marched all night, then asked the LORD for a miracle in front of everybody. (Joshua 10:9, 12) And the writer says there has been no day like it, "when the LORD listened to the voice of a man, because the LORD fought for Israel." (Joshua 10:14) Joshua didn't sit back and say, "God's got it." He showed up tired, worked hard, and prayed big, and the battle still belonged to the LORD.

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery, baker. When something too big for you lands on your counter, do the next thing in front of you, and talk to the LORD out loud while you do it. He listens, and He fights for His people. I used to think nobody was listening back there in that drawer, and I was WRONG about that, so trust me on this one.
